findings.body: Ruby uses the last-defined method, so the class now only exposes a 4-argument (from, to, dimensions, opts) downsize. Calling it with 5 positional arguments raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), causing the ResizeEmoji job (and any other 5-arg caller) to fail at runtime.
findings.failure_mode: Runtime ArgumentError crash in background jobs that still use the old signature.
findings.impact: Ruby uses the last-defined method, so the class now only exposes a 4-argument (from, to, dimensions, opts) downsize. Calling it with 5 positional arguments raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), causing the ResizeEmoji job (and any other 5-arg caller) to fail at runtime.
findings.root_cause: Two methods named `self.downsize` were defined in the same class with different arities; the second silently shadows the first instead of replacing/removing it.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the redundant duplicate definition and update the remaining single `downsize` method's callers (e.g. resize_emoji.rb) to pass a combined dimensions string, or keep both width/height and dimensions-string overloads under distinct method names.
findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 5-argument signature, breaking existing callers
findings.trigger: Any code path that still calls OptimizedImage.downsize with the old (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) signature, e.g. app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at R149 while keeping original 5-arg version at L145. Ruby keeps last definition, so 5-arg callers like resize_emoji.rb:14 `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` will get ArgumentError at runtime.

raw_findings.body: Client validation no longer reflects the admin-configured limit or distinguishes image vs. attachment type: files under the real configured limit but over 10MB are wrongly allowed through client-side checks (later rejected server-side after wasted upload), and files between the configured limit and 10MB that should be rejected client-side are now allowed, causing inconsistent UX and wasted bandwidth.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Incorrect client-side accept/reject decisions relative to actual server-enforced limits.
raw_findings.impact: Client validation no longer reflects the admin-configured limit or distinguishes image vs. attachment type: files under the real configured limit but over 10MB are wrongly allowed through client-side checks (later rejected server-side after wasted upload), and files between the configured limit and 10MB that should be rejected client-side are now allowed, causing inconsistent UX and wasted bandwidth.
raw_findings.root_cause: Site-setting-driven size lookup was replaced with a hardcoded numeric literal, removing admin configurability and the type-based distinction.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep reading the limit from Discourse.SiteSettings (e.g. per type), and if a larger limit is intended to support the new server-side downsizing feature, expose that as a dedicated configurable site setting instead of a hardcoded literal.
raw_findings.title: Client-side upload size check hardcoded, ignoring per-type site settings
raw_findings.trigger: An admin configures max_image_size_kb or max_attachment_size_kb to a value other than 10240 KB (e.g. default 3072 KB), then a user attempts to upload a file whose size differs from the new hardcoded 10MB threshold.

raw_findings.body: The bootbox alert reports an incorrect max_size_kb value to the user, misleading them about the real upload size limit that caused the rejection.
raw_findings.failure_mode: User-facing error message is inaccurate relative to actual server configuration.
raw_findings.impact: The bootbox alert reports an incorrect max_size_kb value to the user, misleading them about the real upload size limit that caused the rejection.
raw_findings.root_cause: Dynamic Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb lookup was replaced with a hardcoded literal.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Retain a dynamic lookup of the relevant site setting (or actual configured server limit) instead of a hardcoded constant for the error message.
raw_findings.title: 413 error message shows hardcoded 10MB instead of actual configured/nginx limit
raw_findings.trigger: A file upload triggers an HTTP 413 (entity too large) response from the web server whose actual configured limit (nginx client_max_body_size, max_image_size_kb) differs from 10MB.

raw_findings.body: The server will now download up to 10MB from an arbitrary remote URL regardless of the admin's configured max_image_size_kb, consuming more bandwidth/disk than intended before any size validation occurs.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Server downloads larger files than the admin-configured policy permits.
raw_findings.impact: The server will now download up to 10MB from an arbitrary remote URL regardless of the admin's configured max_image_size_kb, consuming more bandwidth/disk than intended before any size validation occurs.
raw_findings.root_cause: Site-setting-derived byte cap replaced with a fixed literal value.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Continue deriving the download cap from SiteSetting (e.g. SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes) or a new explicit configurable setting rather than a hardcoded literal.
raw_findings.title: API upload URL download size cap hardcoded, bypassing SiteSetting configurability
raw_findings.trigger: An admin has configured max_image_size_kb below 10MB and a client calls the API upload endpoint with a `url` param pointing to a large remote file.

raw_findings.body: The signature-breaking change to OptimizedImage.downsize (see duplicate-definition finding) and the new retry/downsize loop are unverified, allowing regressions such as the resize_emoji ArgumentError to reach production undetected.
raw_findings.evidence:
if tempfile && tempfile.size > 0 && SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0 && FileHelper.is_image?(filename)
        attempt = 5
        while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes
          OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)
          attempt -= 1
        end
      end
raw_findings.failure_mode: Undetected regressions in downsizing logic and broken existing callers.
raw_findings.impact: The signature-breaking change to OptimizedImage.downsize (see duplicate-definition finding) and the new retry/downsize loop are unverified, allowing regressions such as the resize_emoji ArgumentError to reach production undetected.
raw_findings.root_cause: Behavioral change (new downsizing loop and altered downsize signature) shipped without corresponding spec coverage.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add unit tests for OptimizedImage.downsize's new signature and its callers, and a controller/integration test covering the new automatic-downsizing branch in create_upload (including the attempt-exhaustion case).
raw_findings.title: No tests added for new automatic image-downsizing logic or changed OptimizedImage.downsize signature
raw_findings.trigger: Reviewers/CI run the existing spec suite (spec/models/optimized_image_spec.rb and any uploads_controller specs) after this change; none exercise the new downsize loop, the loop's termination behavior, or the changed OptimizedImage.downsize signature.
